tagline: South along the Missouri, between the river plain and the hills.
intro: Out of South Sioux City, US 75 runs south across the Missouri River plain through Homer, then climbs into the rolling hills past Winnebago and Macy, the seat of the Omaha Reservation. At Decatur it comes back down to the edge of the plain and keeps to it through Tekamah and Herman to Blair, with cropland on one hand and wooded bluffs along the river.

Lewis and Clark came up this stretch of the Missouri in 1804, and the road passes near their old campsites. On a bluff near present-day Fort Calhoun, south of Blair, Clark saw a good place for a fort. Fifteen years later the Army built one.

moments.title: Winnebago
moments.text: Moved here from Minnesota by treaty in 1868, the Ho-Chunk keep a buffalo herd in the village and hold their Homecoming powwow the last full weekend of July.

moments.title: Decatur
moments.text: The village grew up around Peter Sarpy's trading post and took its name from a schoolteacher who came west in 1841, leaving his family and his old surname behind.

moments.title: Fort Atkinson
moments.text: Rebuilt by the state on the bluff Clark recommended, the first Army post west of the Missouri once held a quarter of the US Army.
